# Windows rust-analyzer runtime

BrowserOS builds and ships its Windows analyzer from the official Rust
1.100.0 source at commit
`0ef1bc386059596dada8fb65b50425aab2ea637a`.
The executable is part of the application resource bundle. Windows LSP does
not choose an analyzer from PATH or execute a rustup shim.

## Reason for the patch

The Windows AppContainer acceptance run found a real failure in the upstream
metadata path: `rustc.exe --print cfg -O` could not start because
`Command::output()` selected the global NUL device for child stdin and
the lowbox could not open that device. The fixed-source patch sets Windows
metadata subprocess stdin to an anonymous pipe. Rust's `Command::output`
implementation closes the parent writer before waiting, so the subprocess
still receives EOF.

The patch does not change device permissions, enable network access, allow
Cargo, enable build scripts or proc macros, or bypass failed metadata probes.
The actual AppContainer test must still resolve a cfg-gated helper through
hover and definition and return real syntax diagnostics. A successful build
alone does not establish that acceptance result.

Primary source locations:

- [Pinned metadata helper](https://github.com/rust-lang/rust/blob/0ef1bc386059596dada8fb65b50425aab2ea637a/src/tools/rust-analyzer/crates/project-model/src/lib.rs)
- [Pinned Command output implementation](https://github.com/rust-lang/rust/blob/0ef1bc386059596dada8fb65b50425aab2ea637a/library/std/src/sys/process/mod.rs)
- [Pinned Windows pipe implementation](https://github.com/rust-lang/rust/blob/0ef1bc386059596dada8fb65b50425aab2ea637a/library/std/src/sys/process/windows/child_pipe.rs)

## Reviewed inputs

`source.json` records the exact upstream repository, commit, subtree,
patch hash, original and reviewed lock hashes, and both upstream license
hashes. It also records the original and patched hashes of all five
source inputs: the metadata helper, `xtask/Cargo.toml`,
`xtask/src/dist.rs`, `crates/span/src/hygiene.rs` and
`crates/hir-expand/src/hygiene.rs`.

The independent `Cargo.lock` is generated by Cargo against that pinned
workspace and reviewed with the patch. It retains the url 2.5.9,
form_urlencoded 1.2.3 and rustix 1.1.6 security updates and resolves
crossbeam-epoch 0.9.20, anyhow 1.0.103 and salsa 0.28.5 with its compatible
macros. These versions address the actual sidecar advisory scan, including
the anyhow and salsa memory-safety findings that the scanner reports as
informational warnings. `source.json.lock_updates` records the complete
version changes and package additions/removals produced by the resolver.
Checksums and transitive dependencies are not assembled by hand.

The same patch pins the distribution-only `xtask` ZIP dependency to
`=9.0.5`, retaining its explicit `deflate-flate2` and `time` features and
disabled default features. The exact requirement prevents a major-version
lock migration from silently choosing a later, unreviewed ZIP release. ZIP 9 accepts `PrimitiveDateTime`; the existing
writer now converts the source file's UTC date and time explicitly, reuses
that timestamp for the executable and optional symbols, and propagates
filesystem and out-of-range timestamp errors. The writer's compression,
entry names, permissions and payload handling are preserved.

The fixed source uses ZIP to write distribution archives. The compatibility
probe calls that actual writer with and without symbols, reads back exact
contents, permissions and timestamps, checks local/central header
consistency, and verifies missing-input and invalid-time rejection.
The probe runs only in an isolated candidate checkout. Its injected test is
excluded from the exported source patch and removed after the run. It does
not change the application's acceptance requirements.

ZIP's RUSTSEC-2026-0548 fix provides opt-in checks for untrusted archive
reading. Upgrading the dependency does not make every upstream extraction
default safe. BrowserOS does not introduce an extractor in this patch.

Cargo still builds with `--locked`; the complete analyzer lock is audited
separately from the BrowserOS host lock and has its own software bill of
materials. The optional `profile/jemalloc` dependency retains the
unmaintained `paste` macro crate in that all-target inventory. The Windows
MSVC bundle does not enable the `jemalloc` feature. This warning is retained
in audit evidence; it is not represented as a patched vulnerability.

Primary security and API references:

- [Crossbeam pointer formatting advisory](https://github.com/rustsec/advisory-db/blob/main/crates/crossbeam-epoch/RUSTSEC-2026-0204.md)
- [Anyhow mutable downcast advisory](https://github.com/rustsec/advisory-db/blob/main/crates/anyhow/RUSTSEC-2026-0190.md)
- [Salsa lifetime advisory](https://github.com/rustsec/advisory-db/blob/main/crates/salsa/RUSTSEC-2026-0308.md)
- [ZIP header consistency advisory](https://github.com/rustsec/advisory-db/blob/main/crates/zip/RUSTSEC-2026-0548.md)
- [ZIP 9.0.5 time conversion](https://github.com/zip-rs/zip2/blob/v9.0.5/src/datetime.rs)
- [Pinned distribution writer](https://github.com/rust-lang/rust/blob/0ef1bc386059596dada8fb65b50425aab2ea637a/src/tools/rust-analyzer/xtask/src/dist.rs)

Changing any input requires updating the explicit source contract and
reviewing the patch and lock together. Do not replace the executable with a
downloaded unpatched analyzer or generate a new lock implicitly during a
normal application build.

## Salsa interning compatibility

The Windows build also exposed a source compatibility failure after the
required Salsa 0.28.5 security update. Salsa 0.28.3 removed the interned
assembly callback and the separate `HashEqLike::hash` method. The pinned
analyzer still implemented those internal interfaces by hand; retaining the
security update therefore also requires adapting its hygiene interner.

The reference is rust-analyzer commit
`008951695fa9f66a68ff6e20159e86f626015a3f`, recorded as
`source.json.hygiene_reference_commit`. Its parent has exactly the same
span hygiene source as the pinned Rust tree. This is a limited local
adaptation of the upstream `Option` representation for self-references,
not a wholesale replacement with the later analyzer.

The two derived normalization caches now store `None` for the interned
context itself or `Some` for an ancestor. The three hir-expand construction
sites provide those values without needing an ID-dependent assembly
callback. The existing four identity fields still determine both hashing
and equality; the cache fields do not become part of the key. A
`Lookup::into_owned` implementation converts the key only when Salsa
creates the first value. Re-interning the same identity reuses that value
and its original normalization caches.

The pinned `u32`/root encoding, immortal storage configuration and access
through Salsa remain intact. The adaptation introduces no new unsafe
production code and does not restore the removed assembly API or weaken
Salsa's lifetime and retained-value checks.

The builder compiles the complete analyzer, then runs the patched span
library with `--features salsa` in the same release target directory. All
five existing hygiene tests and three additional tests must be enumerated
and individually pass; zero-test runs, missing tests, extra tests or
ignored tests fail preparation. The additional cases cover self and
ancestor normalization, owned and borrowed cold insertion, repeated-key
cache preservation, distinct identity fields and ID round trips. The
builder checks every patched source and the lock again after these tests,
before publishing any runtime bundle.

Primary compatibility references:

- [Upstream rust-analyzer Option migration](https://github.com/rust-lang/rust-analyzer/commit/008951695fa9f66a68ff6e20159e86f626015a3f)
- [Salsa removal of the assembly callback](https://github.com/salsa-rs/salsa/pull/1314)
- [Salsa 0.28.5 interning and lookup implementation](https://github.com/salsa-rs/salsa/blob/salsa-v0.28.5/src/interned.rs)

## Preparation and reuse

On Windows, from the repository root:

```powershell
pwsh -NoProfile -File scripts/build-windows-lsp-runtime.ps1
```

PowerShell 7, Git, rustup and the native MSVC build tools are required. The
builder installs the exact `1.100.0-x86_64-pc-windows-msvc` toolchain
without changing the user's default. It checks the actual compiler release,
commit and host and records its executable SHA-256. The nested Cargo build
uses a separate working directory, Cargo cache and target directory. Parent
Cargo compiler, wrapper, flags and jobserver environment variables are
removed rather than inherited into that build.

CI can supply `-WorkDirectory` under its runner temporary directory.
The default is a dedicated temporary directory. The builder validates the
upstream commit and input hashes before applying the patch, verifies that
only the metadata helper, the two reviewed `xtask` files, the two hygiene
files and Cargo.lock changed. The six-path set is exact and case-sensitive.
It builds the complete rust-analyzer binary and runs the eight required
span hygiene tests with `--locked --release`. All five patched source hashes
and the lock hash are checked again after compilation and testing. A
normal application build never resolves new dependency versions.

The generated, ignored source bundle contains exactly these declared
resource files:

- `src-tauri/resources/windows-lsp/rust-analyzer.exe`
- `src-tauri/resources/windows-lsp/runtime.json`
- `src-tauri/resources/windows-lsp/LICENSE-MIT`
- `src-tauri/resources/windows-lsp/LICENSE-APACHE`
- `src-tauri/resources/windows-lsp/Cargo.lock`

A cached bundle is reused only after validating its source contract,
executable size and SHA-256, lock and license hashes. Unknown files are not
deleted. The builder rejects reparse points in its output directory chain
or any of the five output files.

`runtime.json` uses UTF-8 without a BOM and LF line endings. It
contains no build timestamp or local filesystem paths. Its top-level fields
are `schema_version`, `source`, `artifact` and `build`.
The artifact records the actual analyzer filename, size and SHA-256. The
build section records the pinned build compiler's release, source commit,
executable hash and target. That compiler is distinct from the user's
installed compiler selected later for sandboxed cfg probes.

## Cargo, development and installed execution

Windows `build.rs` invokes the same idempotent builder before the host
includes the generated manifest. Tauri development therefore does not race
a missing resource, and it retains the existing frontend development server
owner.

`build.rs` recognizes the package-bound Cargo output suffixes
`<profile>/build/<package>-<unit-hash>/out` and Cargo 1.100's
`<profile>/build/<package>/<unit-hash>/out`. The shared pure path helper
requires an absolute path, rejects parent traversal, matches the current
Cargo package exactly and validates the unit hash. It checks only those
two fixed suffixes and returns the existing profile prefix, preserving an
explicit target triple and custom profile name. The `PROFILE` environment
variable reports an inherited debug/release class and cannot reconstruct
custom profile directory names.

Five tests in the existing host test binary exercise this same helper:
old and new layouts, target and custom-profile preservation, wrong
packages or hashes, and relative/traversing/unexpected suffix rejection.
The helper does not authorize filesystem access; the builder retains its
directory/reparse and full runtime integrity checks. The fixed Windows
runtime target remains bound by `source.json` and the embedded manifest.

Cargo's pinned implementation sets `OUT_DIR` from the run unit's
`out_dir_new_layout`; its package path is `name/unit-hash` in the new
layout. The compilation unit's executable can have a different hash, so
the helper validates the shape instead of assuming those hashes match.
See the [Cargo 1.100 build-script environment construction](https://github.com/rust-lang/cargo/blob/3acc79c0c841844675bc53a605922dbfc441e750/src/compiler/custom_build.rs)
and [output layout implementation](https://github.com/rust-lang/cargo/blob/3acc79c0c841844675bc53a605922dbfc441e750/src/compiler/layout.rs).

The validated profile directory is passed as `-ExecutableDirectory`.
The builder publishes the same verified five files into that directory's
`windows-lsp` subdirectory, with the manifest last, and verifies them
again. The cached-bundle path performs this publication too. A direct
`cargo run --release` therefore uses the same adjacent runtime as an
installed release. An unexpected Cargo output layout fails explicitly.

Tests and debug builds use only the fixed repository resource directory.
Release builds use only `windows-lsp` beside the running BrowserOS
executable. NSIS maps the same five source-bundle files to that installed
directory. There is no release fallback to a source checkout, environment
override or external analyzer on PATH.

The host embeds the runtime manifest at compile time. At each selection it
requires byte-for-byte equality with the disk manifest, matches its source
contract against the reviewed source.json, checks the executable length and
SHA-256 under the existing operation deadline, and retains native read
handles to the manifest and executable until sandbox staging finishes.
Those handles also pin ancestor paths and deny concurrent file writes or
replacement. The analyzer is staged without enumerating sibling DLLs.

The user's actual rustc is selected separately through the existing rustup
metadata or a non-shim installed toolchain on PATH. The native compiler file
stays pinned while its normal runtime peers are staged into the sandbox.
Invalid configured toolchains, unsafe paths, missing resources and any
integrity mismatch fail closed. Installing a different external
rust-analyzer cannot bypass the bundled-runtime check.

## Acceptance evidence

Three native bundle tests exercise the actual Windows file handles:
successful verification with write/replacement denial, altered source /
manifest / executable / size rejection, and missing-resource / cancellation
rejection. They never execute synthetic bytes.

The existing real analyzer test remains necessary: its cfg-gated helper
requires Windows target metadata before hover and definition can pass, and
the syntax diagnostic, private snapshot, own-package read and foreign-package
denial assertions remain active. Cargo and code execution stay disabled,
and language analysis continues to report
`compilation_verified=false`.

Record CI, installer payload verification and installed GUI results for the
same commit. These source changes alone do not mark native or GUI acceptance
as passed.
